title: v15.77 active baseline, two verdicts
dek: Research branch only. Not merged to main. An active symmetric baseline can move the center and stay rotationally null. An equal-norm skew baseline is visible. This does not rescue the original v15.76 channel.

claims.text: Primary: ACTIVE_RETAINED_BASELINE_COMPOSITION_NULL_CONFIRMED. Twelve separately calibrated channels use b=ρ+δY with δ=.02. They have nonzero retained baseline action, move their reference states, and keep hidden leakage, while polar rotation stays null through depths 1, 2, 4, and 8. The baseline acts in the polar-symmetric sector. Frozen-reference calibration is not removed. This is not one fixed affine law remaining null on an open neighborhood.

Comparison: EQUAL_NORM_SKEW_BASELINE_VISIBLE_CONFIRMED. Replacing the symmetric baseline by an equal-norm skew direction makes hidden rotational response visible on every tested reference and depth. That contrast is not a universal theorem that every baseline rotational activity forces hidden visibility.
